notes: Read all 25 numbered source lines before editing. TabNav is a small, vendor-agnostic presentational component (a horizontal icon-capable tab strip); its full prop contract and render logic are ported verbatim and only the DOM/clsx/styling layer is re-expressed with React Native primitives.

Imports L1-2: L1 `import { type ReactNode } from 'react'` is kept (ReactNode types the optional `icon` field of TabNavItem) and React itself is added to the same import (needed for JSX + the React.ReactElement return type, matching the PinButton/ContextMenu ports). L2 `import clsx from 'clsx'` is DOM-className tooling with no RN analogue and is dropped — the clsx(base, active?…:…) composition (web L12-17) becomes RN StyleSheet style arrays + per-state style maps. AppText (../../../components/ui/AppText) and the theme `colors` token (../../../theme/tokens) are added for the label text + tints.
L3 blank line accounted for. L4 JSDoc `/** Horizontal tab navigation bar with icon support. */` is preserved verbatim above the exported TabNav function.

Signature L5: the inline destructured prop type `{ tabs: { key; label; icon? }[]; active: string; onChange: (key) => void }` is ported one-for-one but lifted into named, exported `TabNavItem` (key/label/icon?: ReactNode) + `TabNavProps` (tabs/active/onChange) interfaces for native-idiomatic typing; the destructured params `{ tabs, active, onChange }` and every field name/shape are identical to the web. Return type annotated React.ReactElement.
L6 `return (` preserved as the function's single returned tree.

Container L7 `<div className="flex items-center gap-1 rounded-xl bg-white/[0.02] p-1 border border-white/[0.06] overflow-x-auto scrollbar-thin">` -> a horizontal `ScrollView` (the faithful analogue of an overflow-x-auto flex row). The visible frame splits across two style targets: outer `style={styles.bar}` carries `rounded-xl`=borderRadius 12, `bg-white/[0.02]`=backgroundColor rgba(255,255,255,0.02), `border border-white/[0.06]`=1px borderColor rgba(255,255,255,0.06); inner `contentContainerStyle={styles.barContent}` carries `flex items-center`=flexDirection row + alignItems center, `gap-1`=gap 4, and `p-1`=padding 4 (so tabs sit inside the border exactly as the web padding did). `overflow-x-auto` -> the ScrollView's horizontal scrolling; `scrollbar-thin` has no RN analogue -> showsHorizontalScrollIndicator={false} (clean tab strip, the native chip/tab-row convention). accessibilityRole="tablist" added.
tabs.map L8 + key L10: `{tabs.map(t => ( … ))}` preserved; each tab keyed by `key={t.key}` (web L10) on the Pressable. `const isActive = active === t.key` hoists the web L14 active test once per row.

Button L9 + onClick L11: `<button>` -> `Pressable`; `onClick={() => onChange(t.key)}` -> `onPress={() => onChange(t.key)}` (identical handler). accessibilityRole="tab" + accessibilityState={{ selected: isActive }} + accessibilityLabel={t.label} give the generic web button explicit tab semantics; testID=`tab-nav-${t.key}`.

className L12-17 base classes (L13 `flex items-center gap-1.5 sm:gap-2 rounded-lg px-2.5 sm:px-4 py-1.5 sm:py-2 text-xs sm:text-sm font-medium transition-all duration-normal whitespace-nowrap shrink-0`): mapped to styles.tab + styles.label. flex items-center -> flexDirection row + alignItems center; rounded-lg -> borderRadius 8; shrink-0 -> flexShrink 0. The `sm:` responsive UPSCALES (sm:gap-2, sm:px-4, sm:py-2, sm:text-sm) have no RN viewport-breakpoint analogue, so the mobile-first BASE values are used — gap-1.5=gap 6, px-2.5=paddingHorizontal 10, py-1.5=paddingVertical 6, text-xs=fontSize 12 (the values the web renders on phone widths). font-medium -> fontWeight '500'. whitespace-nowrap -> numberOfLines={1} on the label AppText. transition-all duration-normal -> dropped (no RN transition analogue).

Active/inactive branch L14-16: L15 active `bg-white/[0.08] text-[var(--text-primary)] shadow-sm` -> styles.tabActive (backgroundColor rgba(255,255,255,0.08) + a small shadow-sm equivalent: shadowColor #000 / shadowOffset 0,1 / shadowOpacity 0.1 / shadowRadius 2 / elevation 1) with the label tinted colors.textPrimary (styles.labelActive). L16 inactive `text-[var(--text-muted)]` -> styles.labelInactive (colors.textMuted) over a transparent tab background. The inactive `hover:text-[var(--text-secondary)]` is a hover-only TEXT retint whose touch analogue is the pressed state: an inactive tab's label brightens to colors.textSecondary (styles.labelInactivePressed) while pressed, surfaced via the Pressable children-as-function `pressed` flag; active tabs have no hover rule so they remain primary while pressed. Because text colour does not cascade from a Pressable/View to children the way the web button's currentColor did, the tint is applied directly to the label AppText. L17 `)` closes the clsx call — subsumed by the style arrays.

Children L19-20: `{t.icon}` then `{t.label}` rendered in the same order. The optional icon ReactNode is rendered verbatim before the label (the caller owns the icon's colour, matching the ContextMenu icon handling); `t.icon === undefined` renders nothing, exactly as on the web. `{t.label}` is wrapped in <AppText> (RN requires text inside a Text node) carrying the active/inactive/pressed tint.

Closing markup L18 `>`, L21 ``, L22 `))}`, L23 ``, L24 `)`, L25 `}` all accounted for by the Pressable close, the map close, the ScrollView close, and the function close. A TabNav.displayName='TabNav' was added (the parity-tree convention, cf. PinButton/Drawer).

No DOM elements, clsx, document/window, recharts, react-leaflet, framer-motion, lucide-react, or @/lib/cn remain in code — the only mentions are in the explanatory header comment. Imports are limited to react (React, ReactNode), react-native (Pressable, ScrollView, StyleSheet), AppText, and the colors token. StyleSheet keys and per-style properties are alphabetised to satisfy the react-native/sort-styles lint rule. Gates run from apps/native: `npm run typecheck` (tsc --noEmit), `npm run lint -- --quiet`, and `npm test -- --runInBand --detectOpenHandles` all pass.
